title: Laila Sakini + Rebecca Salvadori + Ella Fleck
blurb: Hushed, half-lit songcraft from Laila Sakini alongside video artist Rebecca Salvadori and writer Ella Fleck, the kind of cross-disciplinary Monday only OTO programmes.

title: Strangeness of Jazz: Sly II, w/ Edward George
blurb: Edward George (Black Audio Film Collective) continues his listening-session-as-essay series, this instalment on Sly Stone, with percussionist Crystabel Efemena Riley. Talk, record player and live playing in one.

title: Gwendoline Riley & Leo Robson: The Palm House
blurb: Riley on her new novel with Leo Robson. Her mordant, exact sentences read aloud in a bookshop basement, an ideal Tuesday.

title: The Feminist Texts We Can't Read
blurb: Soo Hyun Lee and Riley Tu on the politics of what never gets translated and how it silences East Asian movements. A properly niche Wednesday evening in Bethnal Green.

title: Lol K: Languid Haunt the Trees (w/ Charles Hayward)
blurb: Lol K curate a woozy evening with This Heat legend Charles Hayward in duo with CJ Calderwood, intergenerational experimentalism in the best way.

title: Fruits on Film: Totally F***ed Up + karaoke
blurb: Gregg Araki's New Queer Cinema landmark with badge-making and karaoke bolted on, the Garden's queer strand at its most charmingly DIY.

title: Adam Bohman / Crystabel Efemena Riley / Sue Lynch
blurb: Amplified junk-object improv royalty Adam Bohman in a new trio with Riley and Lynch, plus Catford to Khartoum. Proper London free-improv lineage.

title: David Lynch Forever: The Straight Story
blurb: The PCC's ongoing Lynch memorial season rolls on with his gentlest film, with Mulholland Dr. and Twin Peaks marathons in the wings.

title: Flare-Up (final week)
blurb: Final week of the group show rethinking the aesthetics of illness and disability, one of the better-reviewed London exhibitions of the summer.

title: Natural Information Society: two-day residency
blurb: Joshua Abrams' guimbri-driven ensemble settle in for two nights of hypnotic, ecstatic minimalism. NIS at OTO is always a pilgrimage event.

title: Darius Jones & Otomo Yoshihide Quintet
blurb: Fire-breathing altoist Darius Jones meets Japanese turntable/guitar iconoclast Otomo Yoshihide in quintet formation, a genuinely rare transpacific summit, over two nights.

title: Evan Parker / Barry Guy / Paul Lytton + Watts / Guy / Lopez
blurb: Two heavyweight trios from the first generation of British free improvisation, with Barry Guy doing double duty, history happening in real time.

title: Friday Night Frights: Roar (1981)
blurb: The most dangerous film ever made: Tippi Hedren, Melanie Griffith and 100-odd untrained lions. Peak cult programming for a Friday night.

title: Devils and Shamans: The Films of Andrzej Żuławski
blurb: A week of Polish cinema's great hysteric: Possession (21st), the doomed sci-fi epic On the Silver Globe (22nd), The Devil (26th) and Szamanka (28th). Not for the faint-hearted, which is the point.

title: Fortissimo Records: ACTION BEAT and friends
blurb: Bletchley's multi-drummer noise-rock horde bring their droning avant-garde guitar army to Manor House. Expect volume and sprawl.

title: Heinous Whining OTO Takeover #3
blurb: The reliably unhinged Heinous Whining crew commandeer OTO for the third time. DIY noise and outsider electronics with zero quality-control filter, in a good way.

title: Within the Around (closing)
blurb: Summer group show closing 23 August. Pair with the Donald Locke on one last NW3 visit before the autumn rehang.

title: Infant Tree: Niloofar Asghary + Augustė Vickunaitė
blurb: Tape-loop textures and quiet radicalism from the Infant Tree label orbit. Vickunaitė's reel-to-reel work is worth the ticket alone.

title: SPACE 4: John Butcher / Yoni Silver / Regan Bowering
blurb: Saxophone physicist John Butcher headlines a multi-set night of new London improv pairings. The SPACE series keeps the scene's bench deep.

title: IKLECTIK x OLI Records: SHHE + Nurah Farahat + Sijya
blurb: The reborn IKLECTIK, now at Peckham Levels after two years dark, links with OLI Records for a triple bill of ambient and left-leaning electronics headed by SHHE.

title: Jasper Marsalis: live coding demo
blurb: Marsalis (a.k.a. Slauson Malone 1) performs live inside his own installation, the closest the exhibition gets to a gig. In-gallery events at Chisenhale fill up fast.

title: Claudia Rankine & Victoria Adukwei Bulley: Triage
blurb: Rankine in conversation on her new book. Book early: LRB events with names this size sell out quickly.

title: Bar Trash: silent horror double bill w/ live score
blurb: East London's trashiest film club goes highbrow-lowbrow: The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari and Buster Keaton's The Haunted House, scored live. The right amount of wrong.

title: Space Day: Interstellar 70mm / 2001 / Silent Running
blurb: A full day of cosmos on the big screen, anchored by Interstellar on glorious 70mm. The rep-house space binge of the summer.

title: All Kaiju Attack: All Stars!
blurb: Two months of monster mayhem: Godzilla, Ghidorah and friends stomping through a properly curated kaiju season. City-crushing on a big screen, as intended.

title: Twin Peaks Season 1 all-night marathon
blurb: The complete first season through the night, damn fine coffee optional. Part of the PCC's Lynch tribute programming.

title: PageMasters Zine Fair
blurb: 40 publishers' tables plus a communal table in Peckham, with workshops Saturday and talks Sunday. The bank holiday weekend's best free browse.

title: Hamid Drake / William Parker / Nicole Mitchell / Pat Thomas
blurb: An absurdly stacked spiritual free-jazz quartet: Drake and Parker's telepathic rhythm section with Mitchell's flute and Thomas's piano, over three nights.

title: Donald Locke: Resistant Forms (final weeks)
blurb: Final weeks for the Guyanese-British artist's ceramics and dark plantation-geometry sculpture. Overdue institutional attention; catch it before the 30th.

title: Lord of the Rings extended editions marathon
blurb: Twelve hours of extended-cut Middle-earth on a bank holiday Monday, a PCC institution. Bring provisions; you shall not pass out.

title: Cinema and State: Films by Nagisa Ōshima
blurb: Nine films from Ōshima's radical 60s–70s run, including Diary of a Shinjuku Thief. Anti-establishment Japanese New Wave in its natural London habitat.

title: System Critical: The Radical Films of Peter Watkins
blurb: The War Game, Punishment Park and the rest of Watkins' furious pseudo-documentary arsenal. Still the most confrontational filmography British TV ever banned.

title: Monica Vitti: Creative Force
blurb: Beyond the Antonioni trilogy: a season making the case for Vitti as a comic force in her own right, with the Italian comedies nobody screens here.

title: Hong Kong Golden Age 1985–1997
blurb: Restorations from HK cinema's imperial phase: A Chinese Ghost Story, Once a Thief, Center Stage and Fruit Chan's Made in Hong Kong.

title: Rio Forever: 50 Years of the Rio
blurb: The community-run Dalston landmark celebrates its half-century with archival gems, 35mm prints and guest intros through October. Support your local picture palace.

title: Elisa Giardina Papa: She Flickered In and Out of History
blurb: Video and mixed-media installation dredging the geological, mythological and political time-scales of the Mediterranean, data-and-folklore excavations stranger than the press text suggests.

title: Nomenclature for the Time Being
blurb: Raven Row's summer group show winds down. The Spitalfields Georgian-house-turned-gallery is always worth the trip regardless of what's on the walls.

title: Del LaGrace Volcano: Sensual / Mutual
blurb: Unseen bodies of work from the 1970s and 80s by the pioneering intersex photographer and queer documentarian. Exactly the kind of archive-surfacing Auto Italia does best.

title: Jasper Marsalis: Still Life
blurb: New commission from the artist also known as Slauson Malone 1, working through gesture, choreography and broadcasting. Chisenhale's commission programme is on a run this year.

title: Sunday School: Container / Will Guthrie + Audrey Chen
blurb: Blown-out techno deconstructor Container duos with percussionist Will Guthrie, a rave-adjacent OTO night that should get genuinely feral.

title: Ak'chamel + Zos Kia
blurb: Masked Texan desert-ritualists Ak'chamel share a bill with resurrected Coil-adjacent industrial project Zos Kia, occult weirdness in Peckham.

title: Not By Lynch: Under the Silver Lake
blurb: The cult conspiracy-noir screened among the Cinema Museum's projector relics. Ideal setting for a film about decoding Hollywood.

title: Cinema of Tomorrow: Goodbye, Dragon Inn
blurb: Tsai Ming-liang's elegy for a dying picture palace, screened inside an actual shrine to cinema history. Rep programming as perfect self-commentary.

title: Tommy Wiseau live: The Room + Big Shark + Q&A
blurb: The man himself returns to Leicester Place. Plastic spoons will fly; football will be tossed. Oh hi, London.

title: Loscil + AM sin
blurb: Vancouver's master of submerged ambient dub brings his grainy, slow-motion drift to the ICA, Sunday-evening deep listening.

title: Katz Mulk + Keiko Yamamoto + Laurel Uziell
blurb: Intermedia junk-electronics collective Katz Mulk top a bill that includes OTO co-founder Keiko Yamamoto. Poetry, noise and performance colliding.

title: Solve-Along-A Murder She Wrote
blurb: The interactive Angela Lansbury phenomenon: whodunnit voting, games and Cabot Cove chaos. A PCC regular that reliably sells out.

title: Loraine James + Eden Samara
blurb: The Enfield producer plays around a new Hyperdub release. Broken electronics with an emotional core. Her ICA shows tend to sell out quietly.

title: Kennington Bioscope: Quo Vadis? (1913) w/ live piano
blurb: The Bioscope crew dust off a 113-year-old Italian epic with live accompaniment. Silent cinema archaeology you won't get anywhere else in London.

title: Abbas Zahedi: SONIC SUPPORT (The Extracorporeal Orchestra)
blurb: Zahedi, Ain Bailey and Tom Harris improvise a grief-listening session in a hospice garden in Clapham. Blankets provided; booking essential.

title: Monika Sosnowska: Weight of Matter
blurb: The Polish sculptor's collapsed-modernism steelwork gets the SLG's main space. Architecture bent until it confesses.

title: Howard Brookner: Films, Archives and the Avant-Garde
blurb: Restored work from the director of Burroughs: The Movie, tracing a lost downtown-NY lineage through Burroughs, Robert Wilson and AIDS-era memory.

title: Lost Reels all-dayer: Women on the Edge
blurb: A ten-hour deep-dive into rarely screened films about women in extremis. The kind of obsessive all-dayer the Cinema Museum was built for.

title: Lavinia Greenlaw & Mark Wallinger: On Difficulty
blurb: A poet and a Turner Prize winner on why difficulty is worth it. The kind of oblique pairing the LRB basement was built for.

title: Ritual Error album launch
blurb: London DIY noiseniks Ritual Error christen a new record in the back room at New River. Expect the Manor House faithful out in force.

title: Koshun Nakao + Rieko Makita
blurb: A quietly intriguing Japanese double bill in SJQ's 75-cap basement, the sort of intimate, adventurous booking this room does best.

title: CTM x ICA 2026
blurb: Berlin's CTM festival decamps to The Mall for two nights of experimental composition, electronics and performance. The best odds-per-pound of hearing something genuinely new that week.

title: SCALD invites Mick Harris (Scorn)
blurb: Napalm Death founder turned isolationist dub scientist Mick Harris headlines SCALD's bass-pressure session. Bring earplugs, seriously.

title: Eternal September: Tennota + Rosa Anschütz
blurb: Noise opera and drone in a chapel setting, with Berlin's Rosa Anschütz on the bill, sacred-space experimentalism done properly.

title: Sing-Along-a Rocky Horror Picture Show
blurb: Full-throated Time Warp with lyrics on screen and props in hand, the PCC's long-running participatory staple. Returns on Halloween itself, too.

title: Evelyn Taocheng Wang: Being Poetic Ruins Life
blurb: Deadpan calligraphic paintings and faux-autobiographical texts land in New Cross. That title alone earns the visit.

title: Five Films from Michael Snow and Joyce Wieland
blurb: A weekend with the structural-film power couple: Wavelength-adjacent rigour meets Wieland's playful materialism. Proper avant-garde rep, increasingly rare in London.

title: Autumn Knight: I Can't Complain
blurb: First major UK presentation for the New York performance artist, new commission included. Expect the exhibition to leak into live performance.

title: Claude Chabrol: Elements of Crime
blurb: Two months of poisonous bourgeois thrillers from the Nouvelle Vague's Hitchcockian, with a companion strand at the ICA (11–25 Sep). Le Boucher with a glass of something red is the correct autumn ritual.

title: A Road Less Travelled: Harry Dean Stanton
blurb: Fifty years of the greatest face in American cinema: Paris, Texas, Repo Man and the character-actor deep cuts. Every screening a masterclass in doing less.

title: LEYA
blurb: NYC harp-and-violin duo LEYA bring their detuned, queasy-gorgeous chamber music to London, one of the most singular live acts going.

title: Paloma Contreras Lomas: Disco Inferno
blurb: First European solo for the Mexican artist, whose tentacular narrative installations skewer class, machismo and paramilitary kitsch. Gasworks' autumn slot is usually the sleeper hit of the season.

title: Wakaliga Uganda: new commission
blurb: The Wakaliwood studio premieres a newly commissioned film on the warrior Kibuuka Omumbaale. Ugandan no-budget action cinema meets the London commission circuit, the autumn's most improbable opening.

title: Nosferatu (1922) with live score
blurb: Murnau's plague-rat masterpiece with live accompaniment, kicking off the PCC's silent-horror run (Häxan and Caligari follow later in October). The right way to open spooky season.

title: Katherine Hubbard: The Great Room
blurb: Large-format photography and a labyrinth of partition walls tracing a mother-daughter relationship. Hubbard's first institutional solo outside the US, arriving via Secession. Preview 6 October.

title: Cecilia Vicuña
blurb: Six decades of the Chilean poet-artist's quipus, precarios and film, her first major UK public survey. The one big-institution ticket this autumn that earns the entry fee.

title: 70th BFI London Film Festival
blurb: The big one turns 70. The Treasures strand is where rep heads should aim: restorations and archive premieres galore.

title: Jeff Preiss: Orchard Documents
blurb: The filmmaker and Orchard co-op founder brings the archive of the legendary Lower East Side artist-run space to Cambridge Heath. Preview 8 October, 6–9pm.

title: Tiny Vipers + Chantal Acda + Red River Dialect
blurb: Jesy Fortino's spectral Tiny Vipers project in a tiny Dalston basement with kindred slowcore-folk spirits, a hushed-room special.

title: Wolf Eyes + Cuntroaches
blurb: Michigan trip-metal lifers Wolf Eyes do two nights at OTO with Berlin gutter-noise trio Cuntroaches, via Upset The Rhythm. First night will sell out.

title: Library of the Occult: Ye Gods (Antoni Maiovvi)
blurb: Giallo-synth auteur Antoni Maiovvi's Ye Gods project headlines a Library of the Occult label night under the Three Crowns, kosmische for the candle-lit set.
